results.title: Continuous batching, chunked prefill and latency-aware scheduling
results.author: zeekay
results.body_snippet: A fast single-user runtime can waste most GPU capacity under simultaneous requests. Token-budget scheduling with chunked prefill, decode prioritisation, admission control and KV-aware batching; prefill is compute-heavy and decode bandwidth-heavy, so the scheduler accounts for both. Keep single-user latency targets separate from datacenter throughput settings. Benchmark: 1/4/16/64/256 simultaneous requests, long/short mixes, p95 TTFT, inter-token latency, throughput per GPU, SLO completion rate.

results.author: Gabriel-Barney

results.title: ttnn.gather and ttnn.nonzero silently return wrong results for BFLOAT8_B / BFLOAT4_B inputs: the kernels compute 1 byte per element from tile_size / tile_hw
results.author: KainanP
results.body_snippet: ### Describe the bug `ttnn.gather` and `ttnn.nonzero` accept block-float TILE inputs (`ttnn.bfloat8_b`, `ttnn.bfloat4_b`). They return without an error, but the results are wrong: - `ttnn.gather` on a `bfloat8_b` input: 2038 of 2048 output values are wrong, ranging from about 1e-20 to 2.5e36. The same call on `bfloat16` matches `torch.gather` exactly. - `ttnn.nonzero` on a `bfloat8_b` TILE input with 4 non-zeros at columns 3, 17, 40, 63: it returns count 2, with coordinates at columns 0 and 32.

results.title: ttnn.operations.moreh.clip_grad_norm with a negative integer norm_type (-1, -2, ...) returns total_norm = 0 and skips clipping when the gradient shape is not tile-aligned
results.author: KainanP
results.body_snippet: ### Describe the bug With a negative integer `norm_type`, the tile-padding zeros are included in the norm: `|0|^p = 1/0 = inf`. The sum becomes inf, `inf^(1/p)` gives 0, and the returned `total_norm` is 0. As a result, `clip_coef = max_norm / (0 + eps)` is clamped to 1 and the gradients are left unclipped. | grad shape | total_norm ttnn | total_norm torch | grad scale ttnn | grad scale torch | |---|---|---|---|---| | (1,1,1,2) | **0** | 0.5574 | **1.0000** | 0.8970 | | (1,1,33,40) | **0** | 0.00

results.body_snippet: Both signing clients follow a same-origin 301, 302 or 303 by rewriting the request to a bodyless GET while keeping the RFC 9421 headers attached.
